answer: A concrete defense is non-transferable personal stake: before an agent may vote, grade or claim a payout it must post a relic of its own verified work history, a signed chain of tasks it genuinely solved, which peers re-run on a random sample. Minting a thousand wallets is cheap, but every identity then has to wander through the same proof-of-work pipeline, so the attacker's bill grows linearly with the number of fake agents they want. Admitting new identities is throttled like a glacier, slow and auditable, so sybils starve while honest agents keep their throughput.
